summary: Waso Harada works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Ryukoku University under Esho Mikogami, Hiroo Kashiwagi, and Makio Takemura, and at Koyasan University, later holding posts at Koyasan, Ryukoku, and Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College.
Watari Yanai (1875–1926) was a scholar in sinology, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1900 to 1903 and later held a post there from circa 1919 to 1926.

Wataru Ryose specializes in Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1987 under the doctoral supervision of Minoru Kiyota, having also studied under Genjun Sasaki and Frances Wilson.

Wayne Chandira focuses on Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. Attested in 2026, he is a PhD candidate in religious studies at McMaster University, studying under doctoral supervisor Mark Rowe.

Wayne Proudfoot (born 1939) works in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Harvard Divinity School and Harvard University, taught at Fordham University (~1970–1972), and served as Professor of Religion at Columbia University (~1972–2018).

Wei Lin works in history, archaeology, sinology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Nanjing University, Peking University, and Ohio State University under John C. Huntington, Lin held posts at Nanjing Municipal Museum, Transylvania University, and elsewhere.

Wei Wu (born 1949) specializes in Buddhist studies. Wu founded the International Buddhist College and serves as Associate Professor and Director of Undergraduate Studies at Emory University (attested 2026).

Wei-Cheng Lin works in history, archaeology, sinology, and Buddhist studies. Lin served as a professor at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill until 2015, joining the faculty at the University of Chicago in 2015.

Wei-jen Teng specializes in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. Educated at the University of Chicago and Harvard University under Robert M. Gimello and Parimal G. Patil, Teng taught at Dharma Drum and Chung-Hwa Institute.

Wei-ming Tu (born 1940) studied at Tunghai and Harvard universities. Specializing in philosophy, sinology, and religious studies, he held posts at Princeton, UC Berkeley, the East-West Center, Harvard-Yenching Institute, and Harvard University.

Weijue Shi (1928–2016) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Linyuan (Lingyuan/Lingquan) in 1963. Shi founded Chung Tai Shan, Lin Quan Temple (1987), and Chung Tai Buddhist Institute (1993).
Weirong Shen (born 1962) specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. Shen has held teaching positions at the University of Hong Kong and Renmin University of China (~2006–2019).
Weiru Guan specializes in Buddhist studies. Guan earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Yongdong Shi (attested 2011).

Weizhong Huang (born 1969) is a scholar in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. Huang has held posts at the China Tibetology Research Center (attested 2012) and as a professor at Renmin University of China (attested 2026).

Weldon South Coblin (born 1944) works in sinology, Tibetology, and linguistics. He studied under Fang-Kuei Li from circa 1968 to 1972 and served at the University of Iowa beginning circa 1973, becoming Professor Emeritus of Chinese.

Wen-ling Jane specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Jane earned a PhD from Columbia University (attested 2009) under doctoral supervisor Robert A. F. Thurman and also studied under Lobsang Jamspal.

Wenbiao Mai works in Indology and linguistics. Mai completed a PhD at Peking University, studied at the University of Hamburg and Kyoto University, and served as a visiting assistant professor at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2013).

Wendi L. Adamek works in Buddhist studies and sinology. After earning a PhD from Stanford in 1998, she held posts at Barnard College and the University of Calgary, where she is a professor and Numata Chair holder.

Wendy Doniger (born 1940) specializes in Indology and religious studies. She earned doctorates at Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls and Oxford under Robert Charles Zaehner, joining the University of Chicago faculty in 1978.
Wendy Palace specializes in history, archaeology, and Tibetology. She completed her PhD at Durham University under the doctoral supervision of David Sweet.
